messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: High error rate (5xx) on hosted inference API in us-west-2. P50 latency 1200ms, 5xx rate 18% over 5m. Paging #eng-oncall. Link: https://ops.redwood.ai/alerts/INC-2109876543

alex: i'm on call until 11:30pt, taking this. starting triage — will need someone to own comms if i have to escalate to execs.

priya: i can take comms. i'll draft a short status and notify affected accounts. ping me any RCA notes.

sam: available as secondary. i'll run smoke checks and tail the autoscaler + proxy logs.

maya: heads up — infra flagged a scaling delay in the us-west dedicated pool about 10m ago, could be related. i'm reaching out to infra now.

alex: first quick checks for everyone: `curl -I https://api.redwood.ai/health` and `kubectl get hpa -n hosted`. paste any big queue numbers here.

sam: running `kubectl top pods -n hosted --sort-by=cpu | head` — a few pods at ~85% CPU. queue depth for inference-proxy is 1200 and rising.

priya: drafting external: 'We are investigating increased errors and latency impacting API requests in us-west-2. Engineers are actively triaging. No account data exposure. Next update in 15 minutes.' edits?

alex: add mitigation if actionable: 'Routing traffic to us-east-1 for affected multi-region customers'. otherwise fine.

maya: infra says autoscaler was delayed by a quota error when provisioning new nodes. short-term workaround: manual scale +3 nodes on the pool. applying now.

alex: executing `redwoodctl scale --pool hosted-usw2 --add 3` — prioritize relief over cost for now.

oncall-bot: ACTION: PagerDuty incident INC-2109876543 triggered -> assigned to alex. Reminder: add incident key to thread.

priya: posted status update and DM'd top affected customers. linked support doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/ops/incident-communication-template

sam: logs show 502s from model-proxy when request payload > 2MB — correlates with large-batch jobs from tenant 'sandbox-qa'.

alex: can we throttle or block large batches from that tenant? maya/infra, can we apply an ingress filter or rate-limit at the proxy?

maya: applying a temporary filter to drop requests > 1.5MB from non-prod tenants. monitoring for impact.

priya: updated external status: 'Mitigation in progress — routing and filtering applied; error rate decreasing for many customers. Next update in 15 mins.' :thumbsup: 

sam: 5xx rate dropped to ~4% over last 2m, p50 back to ~220ms. keeping an eye on queue depth.

alex: handing over formal ownership: i'll stay 7 more minutes then sam will be primary for the rest of the shift. priya is comms, maya stays infra. if anything spikes, wake alex first.

priya: ack. taking comms handover: will continue customer updates and collect logs for postmortem.

sam: taking over driver at 2109876600. starting runbook checklist: runbooks/runbook-latency-spike.md steps 1-6.

maya: note left in infra ticket: manual scale +3 applied; autoscaler quota request raised (#INFRA-742). will follow up in postmortem.

alex: thanks — adding incident to calendar and copying handoff notes to the oncall doc.

priya: handoff summary: primary -> sam, comms -> priya, infra -> maya. coverage gap flagged for ap-southeast if traffic shifts; sam please escalate to oncall-backup if needed.

sam: noted. i will maintain 15-min heartbeats here. :spiral_calendar:

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2109876543 status -> mitigated, monitoring. Please assign a postmortem owner within 24h.
